affected_items.description: Removing support for unneeded filesystem types reduces the local attack surface of the server.
affected_items.rationale: Removing support for unneeded filesystem types reduces the local attack surface of the server. If this filesystem type is not needed, disable it.
affected_items.title: Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled.
affected_items.remediation: 1) Edit or create a file in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory ending in .conf and add the following line: install cramfs /bin/true. 2) Run the following command to unload the cramfs module: # rmmod cramfs

affected_items.description: By monitoring the filesystem state compromised files can be detected to prevent or limit the exposure of accidental or malicious misconfigurations or modified binaries.
affected_items.rationale: By monitoring the filesystem state compromised files can be detected to prevent or limit the exposure of accidental or malicious misconfigurations or modified binaries.
affected_items.title: Ensure AIDE is installed.
affected_items.remediation: Install AIDE: # apt install aide aide-common. Initialize it: # aideinit && mv /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new /var/lib/aide/aide.db

affected_items.description: A host based firewall limits the network services reachable from other hosts.
affected_items.rationale: A host based firewall limits the network services reachable from other hosts. Without it every listening service is exposed to the network.
affected_items.title: Ensure a single firewall configuration utility is in use and ufw is enabled.
affected_items.remediation: Run: # apt install ufw && ufw allow proto tcp from <admin-net> to any port 22 && ufw enable

affected_items.description: Disallowing root logins over SSH requires administrators to authenticate with their own account, which provides an audit trail and blocks direct brute force against root.
affected_items.rationale: Disallowing root logins over SSH requires administrators to authenticate with their own account, which provides an audit trail and blocks direct brute force against root.
affected_items.title: Ensure sshd PermitRootLogin is disabled.
affected_items.remediation: Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config and set: PermitRootLogin no. Then run: # systemctl reload ssh

affected_items.description: Password authentication over SSH is exposed to brute force and credential stuffing.
affected_items.rationale: Password authentication over SSH is exposed to brute force and credential stuffing. Key-based authentication removes that attack path.
affected_items.title: Ensure sshd PasswordAuthentication is disabled.
affected_items.remediation: Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config and set: PasswordAuthentication no. Make sure every admin has a key first. Then run: # systemctl reload ssh

affected_items.description: Limiting authentication attempts per connection slows down brute force attacks against SSH.
affected_items.rationale: Limiting authentication attempts per connection slows down brute force attacks against SSH.
affected_items.title: Ensure sshd MaxAuthTries is configured.
affected_items.remediation: Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config and set: MaxAuthTries 4. Then run: # systemctl reload ssh

affected_items.description: auditd records security-relevant events such as changes to users, sudoers and kernel modules.
affected_items.rationale: auditd records security-relevant events such as changes to users, sudoers and kernel modules. Without it there is little to investigate after an incident.
affected_items.title: Ensure auditd is installed.
affected_items.remediation: Run: # apt install auditd audispd-plugins && systemctl enable --now auditd

affected_items.rationale: The /etc/shadow file stores password hashes. If it is readable by non-root users, hashes can be copied and cracked offline.
affected_items.title: Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow are configured.

affected_items.description: A dedicated sudo log makes privilege use easy to review.
affected_items.rationale: A dedicated sudo log makes privilege use easy to review.
affected_items.title: Ensure sudo log file exists.
affected_items.remediation: Add 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo.log"' to a file in /etc/sudoers.d/ using visudo -f.
